key_insight: In laser–TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel, higher laser power deepens penetration, higher travel speed reduces weld dimensions, and higher current widens the weld while stabilizing the arc.
engineering_relevance: These parameter–response relationships can guide weld geometry and arc stability control for Invar tooling used in aerospace composite manufacturing.
method: Numerical simulation of molten pool dynamics.
High-speed photography of pool evolution and arc behavior.
Evaluation across laser power, welding speed, and welding current ranges.
evidence_signal: Within 5–6 kW, 0.5–0.8 m/min, and 150–170 A, the abstract reports distinct trends in penetration, weld width, molten pool flow, and arc stability.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative validation errors or defect rates, so these trends alone do not establish a production-ready process window.
paper_title: Molten pool dynamic behavior and arc characteristics in laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel
